receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for circulating the Seller’s initial draft. We have reviewed the draft and have the following principal comments on behalf of Buyer:

1. Purchase Price. Buyer is prepared to proceed on the basis of a purchase price of USD 36,000,000, payable at Closing.

2. Closing Timeline. The proposed 30-day outside closing timeline is too compressed given the diligence and third-party consent workstreams. Closing should occur following completion of Buyer’s confirmatory diligence and satisfaction or waiver of all closing conditions, with an outside date 45 days after signing, subject to extension by Buyer for unresolved diligence, consent, or regulatory matters.

3. Seller Representations. The financial statement representation should not be limited to Seller’s knowledge. Please revise to provide that the financial statements fairly present the Company’s financial condition and results of operations in all material respects, were prepared consistently with applicable accounting principles, and that the Company has no undisclosed liabilities other than those disclosed in the financial statements or incurred in the ordinary course since the latest balance sheet date. We would also expect customary representations regarding books and records, compliance with law, taxes, contracts, employees, litigation, and absence of a material adverse effect.

4. Closing Conditions. Please add customary Buyer closing conditions, including accuracy of Seller representations at signing and closing, performance of covenants, no material adverse effect, receipt of required consents and approvals, and satisfactory completion of confirmatory diligence.

5. Confidentiality. The confidentiality provision is generally acceptable, but should include customary permitted disclosures to Buyer’s affiliates, representatives, financing sources, and prospective debt or equity providers, in each case subject to confidentiality obligations.

Please send a revised draft reflecting the above, and we can continue working through the remaining provisions.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for your comments. We have revised the draft to move the parties closer on the principal open points.

On price, Seller has made a meaningful movement from its initial ask and is prepared to proceed at USD 40,000,000, payable at Closing. On timing, we have extended the outside date to 45 days after signing and included the customary condition framework, while keeping the closing mechanics tied to objective satisfaction or waiver of agreed conditions rather than an open-ended unilateral extension right.

We have also expanded the Seller financial statement representation and added customary additional subject areas in a manner appropriate for this transaction, together with Buyer closing conditions for bring-down of representations, covenant compliance, required consents and no MAE. We included a confirmatory diligence condition, provided that any diligence objection must be raised within a defined review period so the closing timeline remains workable.

Finally, we revised the confidentiality provision to permit disclosures to affiliates, representatives, financing sources and prospective debt or equity providers, subject to confidentiality obligations.

We believe this draft provides a constructive path to signing and would welcome a call to resolve any remaining business points.

Best regards,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 40,000,000 for the Shares, payable in immediately available funds at Closing.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur as promptly as practicable, and in any event within five Business Days, after the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Agreement, but no later than 45 days after signing unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing by the parties. The parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to complete confirmatory diligence, obtain required third-party consents and approvals, and satisfy the closing conditions within such period. Buyer shall complete its confirmatory diligence review within 20 days after signing and shall notify Seller in reasonable detail of any material diligence objection prior to the expiration of such period; absent such timely notice, Buyer’s confirmatory diligence condition shall be deemed satisfied.

3. Representations. The Seller represents that: (a) the financial statements delivered to Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition and results of operations of the Company as of the dates and for the periods indicated therein and were prepared in a manner consistent with the accounting principles historically applied by the Company; (b) the Company has no liabilities required to be reflected in such financial statements, other than liabilities reflected or reserved against in such financial statements, liabilities incurred in the ordinary course of business since the latest balance sheet date, and liabilities that would not reasonably be expected to be material to the Company; (c) the books and records of the Company are accurate and complete in all material respects; (d) to Seller’s knowledge, the Company is in compliance in all material respects with applicable laws, has timely filed all material tax returns required to be filed and paid all material taxes due, and is not subject to any material pending litigation; (e) to Seller’s knowledge, the material contracts made available to Buyer are in full force and effect and neither the Company nor any counterparty is in material default thereunder; (f) to Seller’s knowledge, the Company is in compliance in all material respects with applicable employment laws; and (g) since the latest balance sheet date, there has not occurred any material adverse effect on the Company.

4. Buyer Closing Conditions. Buyer’s obligation to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby shall be subject to: (a) the Seller’s representations and warranties being true and correct in all material respects as of signing and as of Closing, except for representations and warranties made as of a specified date, which shall be true and correct in all material respects as of such date; (b) Seller having performed in all material respects its covenants required to be performed prior to Closing; (c) receipt of consents and approvals expressly identified by the parties in a schedule to this Agreement as required closing deliverables; (d) no material adverse effect having occurred since signing; and (e) Buyer having completed confirmatory diligence within the period set forth in Section 2 without identifying a material adverse issue that was not fairly disclosed to Buyer prior to signing and that would reasonably be expected to result in a material adverse effect.

5. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement, the existence and status of negotiations, and all non-public information exchanged in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby are confidential and shall not be disclosed by either party except: (a) to its affiliates and representatives who have a need to know; (b) by Buyer to its financing sources and prospective debt or equity financing providers and their respective representatives, in each case in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby; (c) as required by law, regulation, legal process or applicable stock exchange rule; or (d) with the prior written consent of the other party; provided that, in the case of disclosures under clauses (a) and (b), the recipient is informed of the confidential nature of the information and is subject to confidentiality obligations or professional duties of confidentiality no less protective in any material respect than those set forth herein. The disclosing party shall be responsible for any breach of this Section by its affiliates, representatives, financing sources or prospective financing providers.

receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. We appreciate Seller’s movement and the additions on representations, closing conditions, diligence and confidentiality. We think the draft is moving in the right direction, subject to the points below.

First, on price, Buyer is prepared to move forward at USD 36,000,000, payable at Closing. That price reflects the remaining diligence uncertainty, the need for third-party consents and the limited operating history and financial information made available to date. If Seller can agree to that number, we believe the remaining drafting points can be resolved promptly.

Second, the draft appears to skip Section 4 in the visible text. The Buyer closing conditions appear only as tracked-change text. Please conform the document so those conditions are included as an operative Section 4 in the clean draft.

Third, the confirmatory diligence condition should not be limited to issues that would independently be expected to result in a material adverse effect. Buyer can accept a defined review period, but if diligence identifies a material adverse issue that was not fairly disclosed before signing, Buyer should not be required to close. We propose revising Section 4(e) accordingly.

Fourth, several Seller representations are qualified by Seller’s knowledge. For core matters such as financial statements, liabilities, books and records, taxes, litigation, compliance, material contracts and employment matters, Buyer requires unqualified representations, subject to materiality where appropriate. Knowledge qualifiers may be appropriate for limited counterparty-specific matters, but not for the Company’s own compliance and records.

Finally, on timing, Buyer can work within the 45-day outside date, provided that Buyer has a limited extension right if required third-party consents or approvals remain outstanding and Buyer is not then in material breach.

We are available for a call to close these points and, if helpful, can circulate a marked draft reflecting the above.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
